title: Why Metallic Foil Looks Dull After Stamping

seo.title: Why Metallic Foil Looks Dull After Stamping

content:
A dull metallic result can reduce the premium feeling of cosmetic boxes, wine boxes and gift packaging. When gold or silver foil does not look bright enough, the cause may be the foil, the paper surface or the machine setting.

## Common Causes of Dull Foil

Excessive temperature can reduce metallic brightness. Too much machine force can also make the surface look flat. Rough paper or textured paper may scatter light, so the stamped area appears less reflective than it would on smooth coated paper.

Foil finish is another factor. High-gloss gold, matte gold, pigment foil and brushed foil are designed to look different. Make sure the selected finish matches the expected visual effect.

## How to Diagnose

Stamp the same foil on smooth coated paper and on the actual production paper. If it looks brighter on smooth paper, the substrate is influencing the result. If it looks dull on both, reduce the setting or test a higher-gloss foil.

## What Buyers Should Approve

Approve a stamped sample on the actual paper surface. Color cards and loose roll samples do not show the full effect of the final package.

## FAQ

### Why does gold foil look gray?

Possible reasons include excessive heat, rough paper, unsuitable finish or too much machine force.

### Can higher pressure improve gloss?

Usually no. Too much force can reduce the clean reflective look.
